title: 13 Largest US Public Pensions Book $138B in Paper Gains From AI Stocks
summary:
Domestic equity holdings in 15 AI-linked stocks, including chipmakers and hyperscalers, grew to represent 27% of the portfolios of the 13 largest US public pensions that manage their own investments by June, up from 12% when ChatGPT launched. Those securities generated $138 billion in paper gains for the funds between the end of 2022 and June, accounting for roughly 57% of their US stock gains.

The increase in AI exposure follows political pushback from officials who oversee the funds. New York paused new data center construction and Pennsylvania’s treasurer opposed data-center growth, while California union leaders urged managers to consider AI’s impact on workers even as the state’s $650B fund invested $500M in data-center providers. Total assets across hundreds of state and local public-employee pension funds rose from $5.8T in 2023 to $7.3T in June, per Fed data.

selectedTweets.text:
WSJ: America’s public pensions now depend on the AI industry that the politicians who run them are turning against.

13 large US public pensions booked $138B in paper gains from AI stocks since late 2022.

Those 15 stocks, including hyperscalers and chipmakers, made up 27% of the funds’ domestic equity in June, up from 12% when ChatGPT launched.

That concentration drove roughly 57% of their US stock gains, without counting AI exposure through foreign shares, private equity or private debt.

> New York paused new data centers while its retirement fund’s AI holdings kept climbing.
> Pennsylvania’s treasurer fights data-center growth while overseeing a pension holding billions in AI assets.
> California union leaders want pension managers to weigh AI’s harm to workers while the state’s $650B fund backs data-center providers with $500M.
> New York’s comptroller pressed tech firms over residents’ power, land and water fears while overseeing a fund profiting from those firms.
